account.note: NO EXIT WAS DUE, AND ON THIS SLOT THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE OUTPUT RATHER THAN A THIN RESULT. Fired 12:21 ET against the 12:17 slot, FOUR MINUTES LATE and comfortably inside the 20-minute guard - the FOURTH CONSECUTIVE RUN today to clear its own window, against a 8/12 that lost all nine slots and a 8/11 that lost five. Connector attached and live state read: the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier EXACTLY against the connector list, every other account was discarded unread, and no identifier appears in this file or the commit. ALL FOUR OKLO LEVELS CHECKED AGAINST A LIVE 45.28 BID AND ALL FOUR CLEAR. 2 shares at a 45.1499 average struck 16:21:55 UTC: +0.29%, twenty-six cents of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up a further 19.66%; the 41.54 stop needs it down 8.26%; the time stop is the 8/14 close with today SESSION 4 OF 5, so exactly one session exists after this one. The option position list was queried live and is EMPTY, so no no-fly window closes on anything. Nothing sold, nothing trimmed, no exit specification owed. THE GAIN THE LAPSED SMCI LIMIT COST THIS ACCOUNT HAS LARGELY EVAPORATED IN ONE HOUR, AND THAT IS RECORDED WITH THE SAME PROMINENCE THE LOSS WAS. At 11:21 SMCI was 41.70 bid, 5.20% above the dead 39.64 limit, and this board led its note with the fact that a fill would be +12.36 unrealized on 237.84 - deliberately, because the hour before that it had cited the 8/10 JOBY spec as precedent that a lapsed limit costs nothing. SMCI is now 39.87 bid / 39.88 ask, -4.39% in the hour, +6.01% on the day and just 0.58% above the dead limit: the phantom position is +1.38 rather than +12.36, so 10.98 of the 12.36 is gone. THE SYMMETRY IS THE POINT AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. An hour ago the honest thing was to publish a cost that embarrassed the decision; this hour the honest thing is to publish that the cost was mostly an artifact of the hour it was measured in, and neither reading was ever information about whether not re-striking was correct. A miss priced at 11:21 and a miss priced at 12:21 differ by 89% on the identical decision, which is the strongest available argument that intraday marks do not grade a process. THE SPEC IS STILL NOT RE-STRUCK, AND THIS HOUR'S NUMBER IS NOT ALLOWED TO BE THE ARGUMENT EITHER. 39.87 is a better price than 41.70 and it changes nothing: it is still the identical forced item-2 failure, still 26.2% above the pre-print 31.60 close, still a name with no day-2/3 pullback that holds anywhere in its two-session tape, and an intraday fade off a 41.70 high is not the pullback the rulebook buys. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged for 2026-08-13; this slot's default is no trade and its bar is explicitly HIGHER. Re-striking now because the price came back to where this board wanted it an hour ago would be the same chase wearing a better entry price. BREADTH IS NOT RE-STRUCK AND THE CANDIDATE TABLE BELOW REMAINS THE OPEN'S 09:46 READ, labelled as such. This run quoted OKLO and SMCI live because those are the two names it owed a number on - one held, one lapsed - and did not refresh ten names it has no decision to make about, because a half-refreshed board reads as one timestamp and is not. Provenance re-checked a fifteenth time: the broker returns ZERO equity orders in this account today, so nothing filled and the 39.64 limit is confirmed dead. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending and nothing unsettled; account value 1010.24.

account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. The 900.00 is a deposit I made; the account is funded to about 1000 and the cash is spendable. This answers the deposit and NOTHING ELSE - it is not an authorisation for the OKLO order the 10:46 sync found, which no run here published and which arrived through the same agentic channel escalated on 8/7; that escalation stands open and unanswered. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

positions.note: HELD, AND ALL FOUR LEVELS CLEAR ON A LIVE 45.28 BID STRUCK 16:21:55 UTC. 2 shares at a 45.1499 average: +0.29%, twenty-six cents of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up a further 19.66%; the 41.54 stop needs it down 8.26%; the time stop is the 8/14 close and today is SESSION 4 OF 5. THE FOURTH DIFFERENT ANSWER IN FOUR HOURS TO A QUESTION NOBODY SHOULD BE ASKING HOURLY. The bid has read 45.61, 45.98, 45.16 and now 45.28, so the position has been +1.02%, +1.84%, +0.02% and +0.29% - a 1.82-point round trip that has moved nothing about the thesis, the levels, or the decision. This board wrote at 10:21 that a stop 9.66% away was 'price moving, not a cushion anyone earned', repeated it at 11:21 when the same number read 8.02%, and repeats it a third time at 8.26%: the level has not moved once since the fill and every reading of its distance has been a fact about the hour, not about the risk. THE TIME STOP IS THE LIVE LEVEL AND THE POSITION IS EXACTLY THE CASE IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. At +0.29% after four sessions this has gone nowhere - the thesis has neither worked nor failed, which is precisely what the ~5 session rule exists to close. Tomorrow's close sells it unless 54.18 or 41.54 speaks first, and the 8/10 rule says the time stop is not extendable by conviction. That rule gets tested tomorrow on a position that is flat rather than losing, which is where the temptation to grant one more day is strongest. NO SAME-DAY EXIT TRIGGER FIRES. The option position list was queried live and returned empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything, and OKLO appears in none of the 502 calendar events pulled live across 8/13 to 8/19, so no print lands inside the remaining hold. Size 90.56 on the bid, 8.96% of the account, under the ~10% threshold where the 8/10 rule warns rather than blocks. Provenance unchanged after a fifteenth check: one order in this account since 8/7, tagged agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it, and zero equity orders today. Tagged nuclear, which leaves the second slot of that two-name cap open.

entryWatch.setup: SMCI day-2 post-earnings continuation - the forced spec EXPIRED UNFILLED at 10:30, and the gain the miss cost has now mostly evaporated
entryWatch.trigger: DEAD. The 6-share buy at a 39.64 limit expired unfilled at 10:30 and the broker returns ZERO equity orders in this account today. SMCI is 39.87 bid / 39.88 ask at 12:21 - +6.01% on the day and just 0.58% above the dead limit, against 41.70 bid an hour ago - so a fill would now be +1.38 unrealized on 237.84 rather than the +12.36 this board published at 11:21. Struck at the open: bid 39.61 / ask 39.64 at 13:46:16 UTC.
entryWatch.why: THE COST OF THE MISS HAS GIVEN BACK 89% OF ITSELF IN ONE HOUR, AND THAT IS PUBLISHED AS PROMINENTLY AS THE COST WAS. At 11:21 this board led with the fact that the lapsed limit had cost a real gain - 41.70 bid, 5.20% through the limit, +12.36 on a position it did not own - and it did so specifically because the hour before it had cited the 8/10 JOBY spec as precedent that a lapsed limit costs nothing. SMCI is now 39.87, -4.39% on the hour, and the phantom gain is +1.38. Ten dollars and ninety-eight cents of a twelve dollar and thirty-six cent indictment was the hour it was measured in. THE LESSON IS ABOUT MEASUREMENT AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS SLOT HAS PRODUCED TODAY. The identical decision, graded at 10:21, 11:21 and 12:21, reads as costless, then expensive, then almost costless again. None of those three numbers is evidence about whether declining to re-strike was correct, and a board that let any one of them settle the question would be grading its process on the clock rather than on the reasoning. The 11:21 entry was right to publish the number that embarrassed it; this entry is right to publish that the number was largely noise, and neither statement is a retraction of the other. THE SPEC IS STILL NOT RE-STRUCK, AND 39.87 IS NOT ALLOWED TO BE THE ARGUMENT ANY MORE THAN 41.70 WAS. The better price changes nothing that matters: it is the same forced item-2 failure, 26.2% above the pre-print 31.60 close, on a name whose two-session tape still contains no day-2/3 pullback that holds. A fade from an intraday 41.70 high back toward the morning is not the pullback the rulebook names - that is a multi-session structure, not an hour of giving back an extension - and buying it here because it briefly returned to a level this board wanted at 09:40 is the chase with a better entry price stapled to it. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text, was discharged for 2026-08-13, and this slot's default is no trade with an explicitly HIGHER bar. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT, UNCHANGED FROM 11:21 SO THE GRADER CAN CHECK IT: a genuine day-2/3 pullback that holds, bought there rather than here. It has not appeared, and no limit was placed below the market to pretend otherwise.

entryWatch.setup: Options are available for the first time - the standing spread refusal was about the names, not the instrument
entryWatch.trigger: SMCI 2026-09-18 calls, live chain: the 40 strike bid 3.75 / ask 3.95, a 5.19% spread on 14,793 open interest and 0.544 delta. The 38 reads 4.21% and the 39 reads 5.85%.
entryWatch.why: A CLAIM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED SINCE 8/5 IS RETIRED, AND IT WAS ALWAYS NARROWER THAN IT SOUNDED. Options were refused three-plus sessions running on spread - most recently at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, on the tightest of eight live quotes - and docs/RULES.md records the finding as 'the shape of the universe, not three unlucky picks'. What the universe actually was: SOUN, SMR and UPST, three small low-priced names, quoted at 15-45% of mark. The first genuinely liquid chain this board has pulled clears the ceiling on all three strikes examined, at 36 days to expiry and 0.54-0.63 delta. So the correct statement is that the names this account could afford had unusable option markets, not that options are unusable at this account size - and the 8/10 note that 'no balance narrows a spread' is true and was answering a question nobody should have been asking. THE CONTRACT WAS STILL NOT BOUGHT, ON ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ON THE OLD REFUSAL. One 40-strike contract at the 3.85 mark is 385.00, 38.0% of a 1012.33 account against a 40% ceiling, and the rulebook's -40% option stop puts 154.00 at risk - 15.2% of the account - behind a thesis this run has itself marked forced. Theta -0.0556 a day takes about 10% of premium over five flat sessions and vega 0.0496 against a still-elevated 78.5% post-print IV takes about 17% more on a 13-point decay, so the contract can lose a quarter of its value while the thesis is neither right nor wrong. The 6-share equity risks 19.03 at its stop and loses only on direction. THIS ROW IS THE FINDING AND NOT A PLAN. The next time a liquid chain appears beside a thesis that is NOT forced, the option is genuinely on the table for the first time; recorded now so that decision is made against a quoted precedent rather than against a rule of thumb nobody re-tested.

entryWatch.setup: Breadth is 11 green of 12 and the entry is being taken into it - stated as a caution, not a tailwind
entryWatch.trigger: No level. 11 green of 12 on the bid at 09:46, LEU alone red at -0.12%, with the range running SMCI +5.32% down to JOBY +0.13%.
entryWatch.why: ITEM 2's SECOND SENTENCE IS THE ONE THAT APPLIES HERE AND IT IS RECORDED AGAINST THIS RUN'S OWN ENTRY. 'If the whole list is green 5-10%, that is a wait signal, not a buy signal.' The list is not green 5-10% - the magnitudes run +0.13% to +5.32% and only SMCI is above 4% - so the sentence does not fire on its terms, and this row says so rather than stretching it into a refusal it does not support. What IS true and is worth more than the letter of the rule: on a tape where eleven of twelve names are up, most of any one name's move is the tape, and the part of SMCI's +5.32% that belongs to SMCI is smaller than it looks at 09:46. That is the argument for the catalyst having to carry the position rather than the momentum, and it is the argument for the -8% stop being tight against a name whose own session range is already 4.2% wide. Both are written down before the outcome. THE COMPLEX PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND UNCROWDED. OKLO holds one nuclear slot; SMR at +1.67% and LEU at -0.12% could take the second and neither has a catalyst. The SMCI entry is ai-hardware, a complex this book has never held, so the two-per-complex cap is nowhere near binding and no stop in this book gaps with another. AMD at a 496.00 bid is the only other ai-hardware name on the list and is refused mechanically at 49.0% of the account against a 40% ceiling, which also means the complex cannot accidentally fill from that direction. THE DEAD JOBY SPECIFICATION IS RETIRED FROM THIS FILE. The forced 8.85 limit expired unfilled on 8/10; JOBY is 7.97 bid, -9.94% against it, and has been red against that limit at every one of thirteen reads since. The point is made and re-marking it a fourteenth time adds nothing.
